mcqs.learning_point: Understand the meaning of parallel lines
mcqs.question: Which statement best describes parallel lines?

options.A: Lines that intersect at a right angle
options.B: Lines that never meet no matter how far they are extended
options.C: Lines that cross each other at exactly one point
options.D: Lines that lie on top of each other

mcqs.answer: Lines that never meet no matter how far they are extended
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines are straight lines in the same plane that do not intersect, no matter how far they are extended. Option B states this definition. Option A describes perpendicular lines, C describes intersecting lines, and D describes coincident lines.

mcqs.question: Which pair of lines below are parallel?

options.A: Both lines are horizontal and run side by side
options.B: One line is vertical and the other is horizontal
options.C: One line slopes upward while the other slopes downward and they cross
options.D: Both lines meet at a single point

mcqs.answer: Both lines are horizontal and run side by side
mcqs.explanation: Two horizontal lines that are side by side never meet, so they are parallel. Option A correctly describes parallel lines. Option B describes perpendicular lines, C describes intersecting lines, and D describes intersecting lines at a point.

mcqs.question: Which of the following figures shows parallel lines?

options.A: Two lines that cross each other forming an X
options.B: Two straight lines that are side by side and never meet
options.D: Three lines all meeting at a single point

mcqs.answer: Two straight lines that are side by side and never meet
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines are straight and never intersect, which matches option B. Option A shows intersecting lines, C is not a pair of lines, and D shows concurrent lines, not parallel.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in everyday surroundings
mcqs.question: Which everyday object contains parallel lines?

options.A: A road that splits into two different directions
options.B: The opposite edges of a ruler
options.C: The spokes of a bicycle wheel

mcqs.answer: The opposite edges of a ruler
mcqs.explanation: The two long edges of a ruler run side by side and never meet, making them parallel. The road in A diverges, spokes in C radiate from a center, and branches in D spread irregularly, none of which are parallel.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the meaning of parallel lines
mcqs.question: Line l has equation y = 2x + 3 and line m has equation y = 2x – 5. What relationship do the two lines have?
mcqs.explanation: Both lines have the same slope (2) but different y‑intercepts, so they never meet and are parallel. Option A gives the intercept of line m only, C would require identical equations, and D would need slopes that are negative reciprocals, which is not the case.

mcqs.question: A student draws line p through (0,1) with slope 3 and line q through (2,7) with slope 3. Which statement is true?

options.A: Lines p and q intersect at (2,7)
options.B: Lines p and q are parallel
options.C: Lines p and q are perpendicular

mcqs.answer: Lines p and q are parallel
mcqs.explanation: Both lines have the same slope (3). Since they have different points, they are distinct lines that never meet, i.e., they are parallel. Option A is false because parallel lines do not intersect. Option C would require slopes that multiply to –1, and D would require the same line equation, which is not the case.

mcqs.question: A student says two lines that appear to converge in the distance are parallel. Which response corrects this misconception?

options.A: Parallel lines never meet, even if they seem to converge because of perspective
options.B: Parallel lines always meet at infinity, so they are actually intersecting
options.C: Any lines that look like they are coming together are parallel
options.D: Parallel lines must be of equal length

mcqs.answer: Parallel lines never meet, even if they seem to converge because of perspective
mcqs.explanation: In reality, parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never intersect; the apparent convergence is due to perspective drawing. Option B misstates the concept, C is opposite of the definition, and D confuses length with parallelism.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in everyday surroundings
mcqs.question: Why are the opposite sides of a rectangular table considered parallel?

options.A: Because they are equal in length
options.B: Because they are opposite each other and never meet, no matter how far extended
options.D: Because they intersect at right angles

mcqs.answer: Because they are opposite each other and never meet, no matter how far extended
mcqs.explanation: Opposite sides of a rectangle run in the same direction and never intersect, satisfying the definition of parallel lines. Equality of length (A) is not required for parallelism, C is irrelevant, and D describes perpendicular lines, not parallel ones.
